cards.text: It's the fourth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah, and the LORD speaks to His prophet Jeremiah. Take a scroll, He says, and write on it all the words I've spoken to you about Israel, Judah and all the nations, from the day I first spoke to you under Josiah until today. Friend, that's a WHOLE career, not a sticky note.

cards.question: God wants the people of Judah to hear about the calamity He plans to bring on them. What does He hope each of them will do?
Jeremiah has years of the LORD's words to get onto that scroll. Who does he call to write them down as he speaks?

cards.text: Baruch writes down every word as Jeremiah dictates, and then there's a snag: Jeremiah says he's restricted and can't enter the house of the LORD. Biggest project of your life, finally DONE, and your badge won't open the door.

cards.question: Jeremiah can't go into the house of the LORD himself. What does he tell Baruch to do there?

answers.text: Read the scroll aloud to the people
Hide the scroll in the treasury
Hand the scroll to the priests

cards.question: Jeremiah tells Baruch to go read the scroll at the house of the LORD on a day of ___.
Jeremiah hopes the people will bring their petition before the LORD and turn from their wicked ways. What reason does he give?

answers.text: The LORD's anger against them is great
The king himself asked for a warning
The armies of Babylon are at the gate

cards.text: Baruch does everything Jeremiah commanded him. Then, in the ninth month of Jehoiakim's fifth year, a fast before the LORD is called for all the people of Jerusalem and everyone who's come in from the cities of Judah.
Baruch reads from the chamber of Gemariah son of Shaphan the scribe, up in the upper courtyard by the New Gate. Every person there hears it.

cards.question: Gemariah's son Micaiah hears all the words of the LORD from the scroll. Where does he go next?

answers.text: The scribe's chamber in the king's palace
The gate of the city wall

cards.text: All the officials are sitting there, including Elishama the scribe and Micaiah's own father, Gemariah. Micaiah tells them everything Baruch read, and I bet you could hear a sprinkle drop in that room.

cards.question: The officials send a man named Jehudi to Baruch with a message. What is it?

answers.text: Bring the scroll and come here
Take the scroll to the priests
Stop reading the scroll in public

cards.text: When Baruch arrives, the officials say, "Please sit down," and ask him to read it to them. So he does, and two readings in, this man is officially ON TOUR.

cards.question: The officials hear every word Baruch reads from the scroll. How do they react?

answers.text: They turn to one another in fear
They laugh and wave it all off
They walk out before Baruch finishes

cards.question: After hearing the scroll, the officials tell Baruch they must report all these words to the king.
The officials ask Baruch how he wrote all these words. What does he tell them?

answers.text: Jeremiah recited them and he wrote them in ink
He copied them from an older scroll
He heard them in a dream one night

cards.question: The officials are about to take these words to the king. What do they tell Baruch and Jeremiah to do?

answers.text: Hide and tell no one where they are
Flee from Judah down to Egypt
Come and stand before the king

cards.text: The officials store the scroll in the chamber of Elishama the scribe, then go to King Jehoiakim in the courtyard and report everything. I would pay a whole box of cookies to see the faces in that meeting.

cards.question: King Jehoiakim hears the officials' report about the scroll. What does he do next?

answers.text: Sends Jehudi to get the scroll
Sends for Jeremiah to explain it
Calls for the priests to pray

cards.text: It's the ninth month, so the king is in his winter quarters with a fire burning in front of him, while Jehudi reads to him and his officials. Warm fire, comfy seat, a nice reading, what could POSSIBLY go wrong?

cards.question: Jehudi reads the scroll to King Jehoiakim by the fire. Every time Jehudi gets through three or four columns, what does the king do?

answers.text: Cuts them off and throws them in the fire
Hands them to an official to keep
Tells Jehudi to read them once more

cards.question: Jehoiakim cuts the columns with a scribe's ___ and keeps going until the entire scroll is ___ by the fire.
As King Jehoiakim and his servants hear all these words, they become frightened and tear their garments.
While the scroll burns, three officials named Elnathan, Delaiah and Gemariah speak up. What do they do?

answers.text: Urge the king not to burn it
Help throw columns into the fire
Leave the room without a word

cards.question: Jehoiakim won't listen to those three officials. Instead, he gives an order about Baruch and Jeremiah. What is it?

answers.text: Bring them to read it again

cards.question: The king sends three men to seize Baruch and Jeremiah. But who had hidden them?

cards.text: After the king burns the scroll, the word of the LORD comes to Jeremiah. Jehoiakim had the fire. God still has the last word.

cards.question: The first scroll is burned up. What does the LORD tell Jeremiah to do now?

answers.text: Write the very same words on another scroll
Stop speaking to the king for good
Leave Jerusalem with Baruch at once

cards.text: The LORD also has a message for Jehoiakim, and He quotes the king's own question back to him: why did you write that the king of Babylon would surely come and destroy this land? When your own words get read back to you, friend, the meeting is NOT going your way.

cards.question: Because Jehoiakim burned the scroll, the LORD says he will have no one to sit on ___ throne.
The LORD says Jehoiakim's body will be buried with honor beside his fathers.
The LORD says He will punish Jehoiakim, his descendants and his servants. What does He say He is punishing them for?
Jeremiah gives Baruch another scroll, and as Jeremiah dictates, Baruch writes all the words of the burned scroll again. Many similar words are added to them.

findings.problem: Multiple choice dominates stop 1 by a wide margin: 9 of its 11 choice cards are multiple choice, with only 1 true or false and 1 fill in the blank.

rule.text: No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

findings.problem: Multiple choice dominates stop 2 as well: 7 of its 12 choice cards are multiple choice, against 3 true or false and 2 fill in the blank. Both stops also lean the same way, which repeats the pattern.

rule.text: No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

findings.problem: Baruch first shows up here and is never said to be a scribe, in this card, in card 4 or anywhere else in the walkthrough. The text calls him 'Baruch the scribe' (36:26) and 'the scribe Baruch' (36:32).

rule.text: The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: Nothing on the earlier cards points to a fast, so 'day of ___' tests wording the baker hasn't seen, not meaning they can reason out. With harvest and celebration as the other options, getting it right is luck. This adds to the stop's other discovery questions (cards 3 and 10).

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: This is a where question, but its wrong answers are not real Bible details. 'The prophet Jeremiah's house' and 'The gate of the city wall' are generic. The right answer is also much more specific than the other two, so it stands out.

rule.text: For who, which thing and where questions, wrong answers are real details from somewhere in the Bible, like Joppa when the right answer is Tarshish.

findings.problem: 'I bet you could hear a sprinkle drop in that room' tells the baker the officials are stunned and serious. That rules out 'They laugh and wave it all off' on card 14, which asks how the officials react.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: 'I would pay a whole box of cookies to see the faces in that meeting' is a mild, pleasant line, not a real laugh. The voice here falls short of laugh-out-loud funny.

rule.text: If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.

findings.problem: The card puts weight on the fire burning in front of the king and ends with 'what could POSSIBLY go wrong?' That points straight at the scroll burning and rules out the wrong answers on card 4 ('Hands them to an official to keep' and 'Tells Jehudi to read them once more').

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The question says the three officials 'speak up.' That rules out 'Leave the room without a word' and makes 'Help throw columns into the fire' unlikely, so the baker doesn't have to choose.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: 'Their iniquity' (2 words) is much shorter and sounds more like the Bible than 'Their alliance with Egypt' and 'Their trade with Tyre', so the right answer stands out.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone.

findings.problem: No card tells the rest of 36:31: the LORD will bring all the calamity He warned about on the residents of Jerusalem and the men of Judah, because they did not listen. Without it, the baker misses that the judgment reaches the whole people, not only the king's house.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.
